title: Survival Skills Academy
description: Essential outdoor, emergency, and life skills to keep you safe and self-reliant in any situation.

personal_safety.name: Stranger Awareness
learning_objectives: Identify safe adults
Know what to do if approached by a stranger
Understand personal boundaries
key_steps: Learn the 'safe adult' circle (family, known teachers)
Recognise warning signs: adult asking for help, offering gifts
Practise saying 'No, I'm going to find a trusted adult'
Know your full name, parent's name, and phone number
practice_activities: Role-play with a parent: practise saying no and walking away
Memorise emergency contact number

quiz.q: What should you do if a stranger offers you a gift?
quiz.a: Say no and find a trusted adult immediately

quiz.q: Who is in your 'safe adults' circle?
quiz.a: Parents, known family members, and school staff

personal_safety.important_note: This lesson is for awareness and safety — always practise with a trusted adult at home.

personal_safety.name: Lost Child Procedures
learning_objectives: Know what to do when lost in a public place
Identify safe places to go
Stay calm and find help
key_steps: STOP: stay where you are if safe
Look for a uniformed worker (police, shop assistant)
Go to a customer service desk in a shop
Call out to a mum or dad with children nearby
Never leave with a stranger even if they say your parents sent them
practice_activities: Practise with a parent: what would you do if separated in a shopping centre?
Memorise your parent's phone number

quiz.q: What is the first thing to do if you get lost?
quiz.a: Stop and stay where you are if it is safe

quiz.q: Who is a safe person to ask for help when lost in a shop?
quiz.a: A uniformed shop worker or customer service staff

personal_safety.important_note: Always practise this scenario with a parent or guardian.

personal_safety.name: Online Safety Basics
learning_objectives: Identify safe and unsafe online behaviour
Know not to share personal information
Report uncomfortable content to a trusted adult
key_steps: Never share: full name, address, school, or phone number online
Use privacy settings on apps
If someone online makes you uncomfortable, tell an adult
Recognise phishing attempts and fake messages
Block and report — do not engage with trolls
practice_activities: Review privacy settings on a device with a parent
Discuss: what information is safe to share online and what is not

quiz.q: Name one thing you should never share online.
quiz.a: Home address, school name, phone number, or full name

quiz.q: What should you do if someone online makes you uncomfortable?
quiz.a: Tell a trusted adult immediately

personal_safety.important_note: Online safety rules apply to everyone, including friends and classmates.

personal_safety.name: Body Safety and Personal Boundaries
learning_objectives: Understand the concept of personal boundaries
Know the correct terms for body parts
Know how to say no and report unsafe touch
key_steps: Understand: your body belongs to you
Safe vs unsafe touch: medical, accidental vs uncomfortable
Practise saying 'No, stop, I will tell'
Always tell a trusted adult if something feels wrong
practice_activities: Role-play boundary scenarios with a parent
Practise the phrases: 'No', 'Stop', 'I will tell'

quiz.q: What should you do if a touch feels uncomfortable?
quiz.a: Say no, get away, and tell a trusted adult

quiz.q: Whose body belongs to you?
quiz.a: Your own body belongs to you

personal_safety.important_note: This lesson should be guided and discussed by a parent or guardian.

personal_safety.name: Safe Use of the Internet and Social Media
learning_objectives: Understand digital footprint
Recognise cyberbullying and how to respond
Protect passwords and accounts
key_steps: A digital footprint is everything you post online — it can be permanent
Use strong passwords (12+ characters, mix of types)
Cyberbullying: save evidence, block, report, tell an adult
Think before you post: would you be comfortable if a teacher saw this?
Verify news before sharing — misinformation spreads fast
practice_activities: Audit your social media privacy settings
Create a strong password for a mock account exercise

quiz.q: What is a digital footprint?
quiz.a: The trail of data you leave online through posts, searches, and messages

quiz.q: What should you do if you receive cyberbullying messages?
quiz.a: Save evidence, block the sender, and tell a trusted adult

personal_safety.important_note: Once something is posted online, it may never be fully deleted.

personal_safety.name: Personal Emergency Plan
learning_objectives: Create a personal emergency contact list
Agree a family meeting point
Know emergency service numbers
key_steps: Write down: 3 emergency contacts (name + number)
Agree a family meeting point if separated in an emergency
Know your local emergency numbers (police, fire, ambulance)
Put the list in your school bag
practice_activities: Create a physical emergency contact card with a parent
Memorise two key phone numbers

quiz.q: What is the emergency number in your country?
quiz.a: Varies by country — e.g. 999 (UK), 911 (USA), 112 (EU)

quiz.q: Where should you keep your emergency contact list?
quiz.a: In your school bag, in your phone, memorised

personal_safety.important_note: Update the contact list whenever family phone numbers change.

emergency_preparedness.name: Fire Safety at Home
learning_objectives: Identify fire hazards
Know the stop-drop-roll technique
Plan and practise a home fire escape
key_steps: Identify common fire hazards: candles, unattended stoves, overloaded sockets
Stop, Drop, Roll if clothing catches fire
Plan two exit routes from every room
Agree a meeting point outside
Call emergency services from outside — never go back in
practice_activities: Walk through your home escape routes with a family member
Practise stop-drop-roll in an open area

quiz.q: What should you do if your clothes catch fire?
quiz.a: Stop, drop to the ground, and roll to smother the flames

quiz.q: Where should you meet your family after escaping a fire?
quiz.a: At a pre-agreed safe meeting point outside

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Never go back into a burning building for any reason.

emergency_preparedness.name: Earthquake Safety
learning_objectives: Identify safe spots during an earthquake
Know the drop-cover-hold technique
Know what to do after shaking stops
key_steps: Drop to hands and knees
Cover your head and neck under a sturdy table or against an interior wall
Hold on until shaking stops
After: check for injuries, expect aftershocks
Stay away from damaged buildings and power lines
practice_activities: Practise drop-cover-hold at school or home
Identify safe spots in your classroom

quiz.q: What is the correct response during an earthquake?
quiz.a: Drop, Cover, Hold — get under a sturdy surface and protect your head

quiz.q: What should you do after an earthquake stops?
quiz.a: Check for injuries, expect aftershocks, and move to open ground away from buildings

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Knowing in advance what to do removes panic in a real event.

emergency_preparedness.name: Flood Safety
learning_objectives: Understand flood warning signs
Know what to do if caught in flooding
Prepare a flood emergency kit
key_steps: Move to higher ground immediately
Never walk or drive through floodwater — 15 cm can knock you down
Turn off electricity at the mains if safe to do so
Emergency kit: torch, water, food, first aid, phone charger
Listen to emergency service announcements
practice_activities: Prepare a simple emergency kit list with a parent
Discuss your home's flood risk and escape routes

quiz.q: How shallow can floodwater be and still knock a person down?
quiz.a: 15 cm (6 inches)

quiz.q: Name two items for a flood emergency kit.
quiz.a: Torch, bottled water, food, first aid kit, phone charger (any two)

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Never attempt to cross floodwater on foot or in a vehicle — it is extremely dangerous.

emergency_preparedness.name: Storm and Cyclone Safety
learning_objectives: Identify warning signs of a severe storm
Know how to take shelter safely
Avoid common storm dangers
key_steps: Monitor weather warnings and alerts
Move indoors — away from windows
Avoid trees, water, and metal objects
If outdoors and lightning strikes: crouch low, spread out from others
Do not use landline phones during lightning
After storm: check for hazards before going outside
practice_activities: Identify the safest room in your home during a storm
Create a storm safety checklist with a parent

quiz.q: Where should you shelter during a severe storm?
quiz.a: Inside a sturdy building, away from windows

quiz.q: Why avoid trees during lightning?
quiz.a: Trees are tall and attract lightning strikes

emergency_preparedness.important_note: A charged portable phone and emergency kit should be ready before storm season.

emergency_preparedness.name: Safe Drinking Water
learning_objectives: Identify safe and unsafe water sources
Know basic water purification methods
Understand hygiene when water is limited
key_steps: Running, treated tap water is safest
Boiling: bring to a rolling boil for 1 full minute (adult required)
Collect rainwater if tap water is unavailable
Never drink from stagnant water sources
Store purified water in a clean sealed container
practice_activities: Demonstrate boiling water with adult supervision
Discuss what makes water contaminated

quiz.q: How long should you boil water to make it safe to drink?
quiz.a: 1 full minute at a rolling boil

quiz.q: Name one sign that water may be unsafe.
quiz.a: Cloudy, smells bad, stagnant, or comes from an unknown source

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Boiling requires adult supervision — never leave a fire or stove unattended.

emergency_preparedness.name: Emergency Signalling
learning_objectives: Learn three universal distress signals
Use a whistle and mirror signal correctly
Understand when and how to signal for help
key_steps: Universal distress: three of any signal (whistle, fire, mirror flash)
Whistle: three short blasts, pause, repeat
Mirror signal: reflect sunlight at aircraft or rescue teams
Ground signals: stamp SOS in sand or snow
Stay in one place so rescuers can find you
practice_activities: Practise the three-blast whistle signal
Demonstrate a mirror-flash with a reflective surface in sunlight

quiz.q: What is the universal distress signal number?
quiz.a: Three — three blasts, three fires, three flashes

quiz.q: What letters should you stamp in the ground to signal SOS?
quiz.a: SOS

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Stay calm and conserve energy while waiting for rescue.

emergency_preparedness.name: Emergency Kit Preparation
learning_objectives: Identify essential items for a 72-hour emergency kit
Pack and maintain a kit at home
Know how long to store food and water
key_steps: Water: 3 litres per person per day for 3 days
Non-perishable food for 3 days
First aid kit and prescribed medications
Torch and extra batteries
Phone charger and emergency radio
Important documents in a waterproof bag
Change of clothes and warm blanket
Review kit every 6 months
practice_activities: Pack a 72-hour emergency kit with a parent
Check expiry dates and rotate food supplies

quiz.q: How much water should you store per person per day?
quiz.a: At least 3 litres

quiz.q: How often should you check your emergency kit?
quiz.a: Every 6 months

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Store your kit in an easy-to-carry bag near the main exit.

emergency_preparedness.name: Heat and Cold Safety
learning_objectives: Recognise signs of heat exhaustion and hypothermia
Know how to prevent heat and cold illness
Respond appropriately to temperature emergencies
key_steps: Heat exhaustion: heavy sweating, weakness, cool pale skin — move to shade, give water, loosen clothing
Heat stroke: very high temperature, red dry skin, confusion — call emergency immediately
Hypothermia: shivering, confusion, slurred speech — warm slowly, add layers, call for help
Frostbite: numb, pale, hard skin — rewarm gently, do not rub
practice_activities: Create a heat safety checklist for summer outings
Practise identifying signs using case-study scenarios

quiz.q: Name two signs of heat exhaustion.
quiz.a: Heavy sweating, weakness, nausea, pale cool skin

quiz.q: What is the first action for suspected heat stroke?
quiz.a: Call emergency services immediately — it is life-threatening

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Stay hydrated and seek shade in hot weather; layer up and stay dry in cold.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Basic Map Reading
learning_objectives: Read a simple map key
Find north using a map and compass
Plot a route between two points
key_steps: Identify map symbols: scale, contour lines, north arrow
Practice locating landmarks on a local map
Use grid references to find a location
Plan a simple route between two points
practice_activities: Use a local park map to plan a walk
Identify 5 landmarks on a printed map

quiz.q: What does the scale on a map show?
quiz.a: The ratio between distance on the map and real-world distance

quiz.q: What is a grid reference?
quiz.a: A number pair used to identify an exact location on a map

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Always tell a trusted adult your planned route before going outdoors.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Using a Compass
learning_objectives: Identify the four cardinal directions
Take a bearing with a compass
Follow a compass bearing to a destination
key_steps: Hold compass flat and level
Let needle settle and point to magnetic north
Rotate the compass housing to set a bearing
Walk in the direction the arrow points
Adjust for magnetic declination if needed
practice_activities: Practise finding north in the schoolyard
Walk a 4-point compass course around the playground

quiz.q: What do the four cardinal points stand for?
quiz.a: North, South, East, West

quiz.q: What does the red needle on a compass always point to?
quiz.a: Magnetic north

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Always use a compass with adult supervision in unfamiliar outdoor areas.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Weather Awareness
learning_objectives: Read basic weather signs in nature
Understand cloud types and what they predict
Plan outdoor activities safely around weather
key_steps: Cumulus clouds = fair weather; cumulonimbus = thunderstorm approaching
Red sky at night = fair tomorrow; red sky in morning = weather warning
Wind direction changes can signal incoming storms
Check a reliable weather app before outdoor plans
practice_activities: Observe and sketch the clouds each day for a week
Compare predictions to actual weather

quiz.q: What do dark cumulonimbus clouds indicate?
quiz.a: Thunderstorm approaching

quiz.q: What does a red sky in the morning indicate?
quiz.a: Possible bad weather ahead (sailor's warning)

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Weather forecasting apps are your best tool — always check before outdoor activities.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Safe Hiking Basics
learning_objectives: Plan a safe day hike
Pack essential items
Follow trail safety rules
key_steps: Always hike with a group and tell an adult your route
Pack: water, snacks, first aid, sunscreen, torch, map
Stay on marked trails
Turn around if the weather changes or you feel uncertain
Leave no trace: take litter home
practice_activities: Plan a hypothetical day hike using a trail map
Pack a trial hiking day bag at home

quiz.q: Name three things to pack for a day hike.
quiz.a: Water, snacks, first aid kit, sunscreen, map, torch (any three)

quiz.q: What should you do if the weather changes on a hike?
quiz.a: Turn around and return to safety immediately

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Always hike with a responsible adult and inform others of your planned route.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Camping Basics
learning_objectives: Set up a simple tent
Stay safe and warm overnight outdoors
Follow campsite rules and leave no trace
key_steps: Choose a flat, sheltered campsite away from water
Set up tent: insert poles, clip on body, peg out guy ropes
Sleep in layers: moisture-wicking base, warm mid, wind-resistant shell
Keep food sealed to avoid attracting wildlife
Leave no trace: bury waste, pack litter
practice_activities: Set up a tent in the garden with adult supervision
Practise packing a camping bag with the right layers

quiz.q: Where should you not set up a tent?
quiz.a: In a low-lying area prone to flooding or under dead trees

quiz.q: Why seal food when camping?
quiz.a: To avoid attracting animals to your campsite

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Always camp with experienced adults and inform others of your location.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Wildlife Awareness
learning_objectives: Identify common local wildlife
Know safe distances from wild animals
Respond calmly to wildlife encounters
key_steps: Observe wildlife from a distance — never feed wild animals
Make noise on trails to avoid surprising animals
If confronted by a large animal: stay calm, back away slowly, do not run
Recognise local hazardous plants and insects
Never handle an unknown animal — even if it appears tame
practice_activities: Research local wildlife that live in your region
Visit a nature park and practise identifying animals from a distance

quiz.q: What should you do if you encounter a large wild animal?
quiz.a: Stay calm, back away slowly, do not run or make sudden movements

quiz.q: Why should you never feed wild animals?
quiz.a: It makes them dependent on humans and can make them aggressive

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Enjoy wildlife from a respectful distance — do not disturb natural behaviours.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Basic Rope Knots
learning_objectives: Tie three essential knots correctly
Know what each knot is used for
Untie knots safely
key_steps: Square knot: joining two ropes of equal thickness
Bowline: making a fixed loop
Cleat hitch: securing a rope to a post
Practise each knot until fluent from memory
practice_activities: Practise each knot 5 times until you can tie them without instructions
Use rope to practise hanging a simple tarp shelter

quiz.q: What is a bowline knot used for?
quiz.a: Making a fixed loop that does not slip

quiz.q: What is a square knot used for?
quiz.a: Joining two ropes of equal thickness together

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Practise knots with adult supervision — rope safety is important.

health_and_hygiene.name: Handwashing and Hygiene
learning_objectives: Wash hands correctly using 7 steps
Know when to wash hands
Understand how germs spread
key_steps: Wet hands with clean water
Apply soap and lather for 20 seconds
Scrub all surfaces including between fingers and thumbs
Rinse thoroughly
Dry with a clean towel or air dry
Wash before eating, after toilet, after touching animals, after sneezing
practice_activities: Practise 7-step handwashing technique
Time yourself: 20 seconds of scrubbing

quiz.q: How long should you scrub your hands with soap?
quiz.a: At least 20 seconds

quiz.q: Name two times you should wash your hands.
quiz.a: Before eating, after using the toilet, after touching animals, after sneezing (any two)

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Proper handwashing is one of the most effective ways to prevent illness.

health_and_hygiene.name: Food Safety and Storage
learning_objectives: Identify safe food storage temperatures
Recognise signs of spoiled food
Handle raw and cooked food safely
key_steps: Keep fridge below 5°C and freezer below -18°C
Store raw meat on the bottom shelf of the fridge
Never leave cooked food at room temperature for more than 2 hours
Signs of spoilage: mould, unusual smell, slimy texture, swollen packaging
Wash hands and surfaces before and after handling raw meat
practice_activities: Check fridge temperature at home
Identify which items in a fridge are correctly stored

quiz.q: What temperature should a fridge be kept at?
quiz.a: Below 5°C

quiz.q: Name one sign that food may be spoiled.
quiz.a: Mould, unusual smell, slimy texture, or swollen packaging

health_and_hygiene.important_note: When in doubt, throw it out — food poisoning can be very serious.

health_and_hygiene.name: Hygiene in Emergencies
learning_objectives: Maintain hygiene when normal facilities are unavailable
Purify water when clean water is unavailable
Prevent disease spread in emergency conditions
key_steps: Use hand sanitiser if soap and water unavailable
Use wet wipes to clean wounds if running water is not available
Dispose of waste safely away from water sources and sleeping areas
Signal for help rather than trying to find food or water in unknown terrain
Boil water if uncertain about safety (adult required)
practice_activities: Pack a hygiene kit for emergency use (list items with a parent)
Practise waterless handwashing with hand sanitiser

quiz.q: What can you use to clean hands when there is no water?
quiz.a: Alcohol-based hand sanitiser (at least 60% alcohol)

quiz.q: Where should you dispose of waste in an emergency outdoor situation?
quiz.a: At least 60 metres from water sources and sleeping areas

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Good hygiene prevents disease which is a leading cause of harm in emergencies.

health_and_hygiene.name: Insect and Animal Bite Safety
learning_objectives: Identify common dangerous insects and animals in your region
Treat minor insect bites and stings correctly
Know when to seek medical help
key_steps: Bee sting: remove stinger by scraping (not squeezing), wash, apply ice
Mosquito: apply repellent, wear long sleeves at dusk
Tick: use tweezers to remove close to skin, clean area, monitor for rash
Jellyfish: rinse with seawater (not fresh water), apply heat
Seek medical help if: severe swelling, difficulty breathing, unknown bite
practice_activities: Identify local insects that require caution
Practise removing a simulated tick with tweezers

quiz.q: How do you remove a bee stinger?
quiz.a: Scrape it out sideways — do not squeeze it

quiz.q: When must you seek medical help after a bite?
quiz.a: Severe swelling, difficulty breathing, or an unknown bite

health_and_hygiene.important_note: For severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis), call emergency services immediately.

health_and_hygiene.name: Backpack Preparation for Emergencies
learning_objectives: Pack a grab bag for evacuation
Prioritise essential items
Maintain and update the bag regularly
key_steps: Bag: sturdy, comfortable backpack
Water bottle and purification tablets
3 days of non-perishable snacks
Basic first aid kit
Torch and spare batteries
Phone charger (power bank)
Spare clothing and rain cover
Copy of emergency contacts and ID
practice_activities: Pack a real grab bag at home with a parent
Review and update contents every 6 months

quiz.q: What is a 'grab bag'?
quiz.a: A pre-packed backpack containing essentials for emergency evacuation

quiz.q: How often should you update your grab bag?
quiz.a: Every 6 months — check food expiry and battery condition

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Keep your grab bag near the main exit so it is easy to take when leaving quickly.

home_and_road_safety.name: Road Safety Basics
learning_objectives: Cross roads safely
Identify road hazards
Understand traffic signals
key_steps: Always use a crossing or pedestrian crossing
Look right-left-right before crossing (left-right-left if driving on right)
Make eye contact with drivers before crossing
Never use phones while crossing
Understand: green man = cross, red man = wait
practice_activities: Practise road crossing with a parent at a real crossing
Identify safe crossing points in your local area

quiz.q: What should you do before stepping onto the road?
quiz.a: Look right, left, right (or left, right, left depending on country) and check all vehicles have stopped

quiz.q: What does the red traffic light mean?
quiz.a: Stop — vehicles must wait

home_and_road_safety.important_note: Always cross with an adult until you are confident in road safety.

home_and_road_safety.name: Bicycle Safety
learning_objectives: Wear a properly fitted helmet
Follow road rules on a bicycle
Be visible to drivers
key_steps: Always wear a correctly fitted helmet
Check brakes and tyres before riding
Ride on the correct side of the road
Use hand signals for turning
Wear bright or reflective clothing
Use lights when riding in low light
practice_activities: Fit a helmet correctly with a parent
Practise hand signals for left and right turn

quiz.q: Why must you wear a helmet when cycling?
quiz.a: It protects your head from serious injury in a fall or collision

quiz.q: What hand signal means 'I am turning left'?
quiz.a: Extend left arm straight out to the side

home_and_road_safety.important_note: Always cycle with adult supervision until you demonstrate road safety competence.

home_and_road_safety.name: Home Safety Hazard Check
learning_objectives: Identify common home hazards
Report hazards to an adult
Understand how accidents happen at home
key_steps: Trip hazards: loose rugs, cluttered stairways, cables across walkways
Electrical: never use devices near water, do not overload sockets
Kitchen: hot surfaces, sharp knives — always ask adult
Chemicals: keep cleaning products out of reach and locked
Window safety: do not climb on furniture near windows
practice_activities: Walk through your home with a parent and identify 5 hazards
Create a home hazard checklist

quiz.q: Name two home trip hazards.
quiz.a: Loose rugs, cluttered stairways, cables on the floor (any two)

quiz.q: Why should cleaning products be stored in a locked cupboard?
quiz.a: They are toxic and dangerous if swallowed or touched by young children

home_and_road_safety.important_note: Most home accidents are preventable — regular safety checks save lives.

home_and_road_safety.name: Public Transport Safety
learning_objectives: Travel safely on public transport
Know what to do if separated from a group
Stay alert to surroundings
key_steps: Wait behind the yellow line on platforms
Let passengers exit before boarding
Hold a fixed support while the vehicle is moving
Keep bag in front and valuables out of sight
Know your stop in advance
If lost: find a station staff member or uniformed officer
practice_activities: Plan a journey using a local transport map
Practise identifying safe waiting areas at a bus stop or station

quiz.q: Where should you stand while waiting for a train or bus?
quiz.a: Behind the safety line, away from the edge

quiz.q: What should you do if you get separated from your group on public transport?
quiz.a: Stay at the last stop, find station staff, or call a trusted adult

home_and_road_safety.important_note: Share your travel plan with a trusted adult before travelling.

home_and_road_safety.name: Water Safety
learning_objectives: Know safe swimming rules
Recognise drowning signs
Respond safely to a water emergency
key_steps: Never swim alone
Only swim in supervised areas with lifeguards
If someone is in trouble: throw, don't go (throw a rope, ring, or float)
Call emergency services immediately
Learn to float on your back to conserve energy if struggling in water
practice_activities: Practise floating on your back in a swimming pool with adult supervision
Identify safety equipment at your local pool or beach

quiz.q: What should you do if you see someone in trouble in the water?
quiz.a: Throw something that floats, call for help — do not jump in

quiz.q: What swimming technique helps you conserve energy if you are tired in water?
quiz.a: Floating on your back

home_and_road_safety.important_note: Always swim with adult supervision and follow lifeguard instructions.

mental_resilience.name: Managing Stress
learning_objectives: Identify personal stress triggers
Use three stress-management techniques
Build a personal stress toolkit
key_steps: Identify: what makes you feel stressed?
Technique 1: deep breathing (4-4-4)
Technique 2: progressive muscle relaxation (tense and release)
Technique 3: physical activity — walk, run, stretch
Write or draw about stressful feelings to process them
practice_activities: Keep a 1-week stress journal
Practise one stress-management technique each day

quiz.q: Name two signs of stress.
quiz.a: Headache, irritability, difficulty sleeping, stomach ache, worry

quiz.q: Name one healthy stress management technique.
quiz.a: Deep breathing, exercise, journalling, talking to someone (any one)

mental_resilience.important_note: Stress is normal — what matters is how you manage it.

mental_resilience.name: Emotional Regulation
learning_objectives: Name and identify emotions
Use the pause-breathe-respond strategy
Choose a healthy response to strong emotions
key_steps: Identify emotions: angry, anxious, sad, overwhelmed
Pause: recognise the emotion before acting
Breathe: use 4-4-4 breathing to create space
Respond: choose a healthy action rather than reacting impulsively
Talk to a trusted adult if emotions feel overwhelming
practice_activities: Emotion check-in each morning this week
Practise the pause-breathe-respond sequence with a partner

quiz.q: What is the pause-breathe-respond sequence?
quiz.a: Pause to recognise the emotion, breathe to calm down, then choose a thoughtful response

quiz.q: Who should you talk to if emotions feel overwhelming?
quiz.a: A trusted adult: parent, teacher, or school counsellor

mental_resilience.important_note: All emotions are valid — it is what you do with them that matters.

mental_resilience.name: Seeking Help and Building Support
learning_objectives: Identify people to ask for help
Understand that asking for help is strength not weakness
Know where to get help in different situations
key_steps: Build your support network: list trusted people you can talk to
Understand that struggling is normal and seeking help is brave
Different help for different problems: teacher, parent, counsellor, helpline
Know your country's youth helpline number
practice_activities: Draw your support network: family, friends, teachers, community
Practise asking for help in a low-stakes situation this week

quiz.q: Is asking for help a sign of weakness?
quiz.a: No — asking for help is a sign of courage and self-awareness

quiz.q: Who can you turn to if you feel unsafe or very upset?
quiz.a: Parent, trusted teacher, school counsellor, or a youth helpline

mental_resilience.important_note: You do not need to handle everything alone — support is always available.

mental_resilience.name: Teamwork in Emergency Situations
learning_objectives: Communicate clearly under pressure
Assign roles within a group
Trust and support team members
key_steps: Clear communication: say what you see, say what you need
Assign roles: one calls for help, one monitors the situation, one provides first aid if trained
Stay calm: panic spreads — focused calm is contagious
Debrief after the emergency to learn from the experience
practice_activities: Role-play an emergency response with classmates
Assign roles and practise clear communication under a simulated scenario

quiz.q: Why is clear communication important in an emergency?
quiz.a: It prevents confusion and ensures everyone acts on the same information

quiz.q: What is debriefing?
quiz.a: Discussing what happened after an event to learn and improve

mental_resilience.important_note: A calm leader improves outcomes for everyone in an emergency.

mental_resilience.name: Building Resilience and Coping with Failure
learning_objectives: Understand that failure is part of learning
Use a growth mindset to reframe setbacks
Build personal resilience habits
key_steps: Define resilience: bouncing back from setbacks
Growth mindset: 'I cannot do this YET' — effort changes ability
Reframe failure: what did I learn? What will I do differently?
Build habits: sleep, exercise, connection, purpose
Reflect on a past challenge you overcame — what helped?
practice_activities: Write about a time you failed and what you learned
Create a personal resilience action plan

quiz.q: What is a growth mindset?
quiz.a: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning

quiz.q: Name two habits that build resilience.
quiz.a: Regular sleep, exercise, social connection, mindfulness, purposeful goals (any two)

mental_resilience.important_note: Every expert was once a beginner — resilience is built one challenge at a time.
